Cross-cutting helpers (rotations, functions, ship_physics)¶

Three modules of shared helper functions: frame rotations, a general geometry/propagation/IO toolbox, and the ship-RCS shapes.

Rotations¶

Summary¶

rotations builds the chain of frames that turns an ECI direction into the antenna frame, so the antenna model can look up gain. The chain is ECI -> VNC -> body -> antenna:

  • VNC (Velocity-Normal-Cross-track) is the orbit frame, built from the satellite’s position and velocity.

  • the satellite attitude quaternion rotates VNC into the body frame;

  • a fixed mounting rotation takes the body frame to the antenna frame.

A direction is transformed as v_antenna = R_eci_to_antenna @ v_eci; the reverse is the transpose.

functions.rotations.quat_to_rotation_matrix(q)[source]¶

Convert a quaternion [w, x, y, z] to a 3x3 rotation matrix.

Parameters:

q (list) – Quaternion as [w, x, y, z].

Returns:

Rotation matrix, shape (3, 3).

Return type:

numpy.ndarray

functions.rotations.build_vnc_frame(r_eci, v_eci)[source]¶

Build the VNC (Velocity-Normal-Cross-track) frame from a satellite state in ECI.

Returns the 3x3 rotation matrix R_eci_to_vnc such that v_vnc = R_eci_to_vnc @ v_eci. The rows are the V, N, C unit vectors expressed in ECI.

Parameters:

  • r_eci (numpy.ndarray) – Satellite position in ECI [m], shape (3,).

  • v_eci (numpy.ndarray) – Satellite velocity in ECI [m/s], shape (3,).

Returns:

The rotation matrix, or None for a degenerate state (zero velocity / position, or position parallel to velocity so the orbit normal is undefined).

Return type:

numpy.ndarray or None

functions.rotations.eci_to_antenna_rotation(R_eci_to_vnc, q_sat, R_body_to_vnc, R_antenna_to_body)[source]¶

Compose the full ECI-to-antenna rotation from the VNC frame and the attitude / mounting matrices.

Chain: ECI -> VNC -> body -> antenna. Vector-coordinate-transform convention, so v_antenna = R_eci_to_antenna @ v_eci and the reverse rotation is the transpose.

Parameters:

  • R_eci_to_vnc (numpy.ndarray) – From build_vnc_frame(), shape (3, 3).

  • q_sat (numpy.ndarray or None) – Attitude quaternion [w, x, y, z] (default identity).

  • R_body_to_vnc (numpy.ndarray) – Body-to-VNC rotation (Constants.R_body_to_vnc_normal).

  • R_antenna_to_body (numpy.ndarray) – Antenna-to-body mounting rotation (RxAntenna.R_antenna_to_body).

Returns:

The full ECI-to-antenna rotation, shape (3, 3).

Return type:

numpy.ndarray

functions.rotations.eci_to_antenna_rotation_from_state(sat_pos_eci, sat_vel_eci, antenna, q_sat=None)[source]¶

Build VNC from the satellite state and compose the full ECI→antenna rotation in one call. Returns None if the VNC frame is degenerate.

Parameters:

  • sat_pos_eci (ndarray)

  • sat_vel_eci (ndarray)

  • q_sat (ndarray | None)

Return type:

ndarray | None

Ship physics¶

Summary¶

ship_physics provides two idealised radar shapes used to model a ship as a hard target: a scalar physical-optics flat plate (a hull side or deck) and an engineering surrogate for a 90-degree dihedral.

The flat plate peaks when its normal bisects the transmitter and receiver directions, with the cross-section

(32)¶\[\sigma_\mathrm{plate} = \frac{4\pi A^2}{\lambda^2}\cos^2\left(\alpha\right)\; \operatorname{sinc}^2(u_1)\,\operatorname{sinc}^2(u_2),\]

for plate area \(A\), the angle \(\alpha\) between the plate normal and the bistatic bisector, and the edge form-factor arguments \(u_i\). The dihedral peaks at retroreflection (signal returned straight back),

(33)¶\[\sigma_\mathrm{dihedral} = \frac{8\pi (LH)^2}{\lambda^2}\,\operatorname{sinc}^2(u_\mathrm{edge}),\]

for edge length \(L\) and leg height \(H\). Both are zero when the shape faces away (back-face / wedge visibility).

Bistatic RCS helpers for ship-as-target modelling.

flat_plate_rcs: Scalar physical-optics RCS of a rectangular PEC plate with back-face culling. dihedral_rcs: Idealised bistatic RCS surrogate for a 90-deg dihedral with wedge visibility.

Both functions are vectorised over the per-sample axis (n samples per call) and operate on direction unit vectors / range scalars; they have no dependence on the simulator’s frame choices beyond a consistent reference frame for all input vectors.

functions.ship_physics.flat_plate_rcs(n_plate, edge_1, edge_2, length_edge_1_m, length_edge_2_m, n_tx2s, n_s2rx, wavelength_m)[source]¶

Bistatic RCS of a rectangular PEC flat plate via physical optics.

The cross-section is sigma = (4 pi A^2 / lambda^2) * cos^2(alpha) * sinc^2(u_1) * sinc^2(u_2) * visibility, with plate area A = length_edge_1_m * length_edge_2_m, alpha the angle between the plate normal and the bistatic bisector of n_s2rx - n_tx2s, u_i = length_edge_i_m / lambda * (n_tx2s - n_s2rx) . edge_i, and a back-face visibility that is 1 only when the plate normal faces both Tx and Rx.

Parameters:

  • n_plate (numpy.ndarray) – Outward plate normal (unit), shape (n, 3).

  • edge_1 (numpy.ndarray) – Two perpendicular in-plane edge directions (unit), shape (n, 3).

  • edge_2 (numpy.ndarray) – Two perpendicular in-plane edge directions (unit), shape (n, 3).

  • length_edge_1_m (float) – Plate lengths along edge_1 / edge_2 [m].

  • length_edge_2_m (float) – Plate lengths along edge_1 / edge_2 [m].

  • n_tx2s (numpy.ndarray) – Tx-to-surface and surface-to-Rx unit directions, shape (n, 3).

  • n_s2rx (numpy.ndarray) – Tx-to-surface and surface-to-Rx unit directions, shape (n, 3).

  • wavelength_m (float) – Carrier wavelength [m].

Returns:

Per-sample plate RCS [m^2], shape (n,); 0 when not visible.

Return type:

numpy.ndarray

functions.ship_physics.dihedral_rcs(edge_hat, leg_1_normal, leg_2_normal, length_edge_m, leg_dimension_m, n_tx2s, n_s2rx, wavelength_m)[source]¶

Idealised bistatic RCS of a 90-degree dihedral corner reflector.

The cross-section is sigma = (8 pi (L H)^2 / lambda^2) * sinc^2(u_edge) * wedge_visibility, with edge length L = length_edge_m, leg height H = leg_dimension_m, and u_edge = L / lambda * (n_s2rx + n_tx2s) . edge_hat (zero at ideal retroreflection, n_s2rx == -n_tx2s, giving the peak). The wedge visibility is 1 only when the directions to both Tx and Rx lie inside the open corner quadrant (positive along both leg normals); outside it the dihedral shadows itself. This scalar surrogate omits the full angular/polarimetric finite-leg response and sea-surface coupling, so it should not be treated as a calibrated absolute ship RCS.

Parameters:

  • edge_hat (numpy.ndarray) – Unit vector along the dihedral edge, shape (n, 3).

  • leg_1_normal (numpy.ndarray) – Outward unit normals of the two legs, shape (n, 3).

  • leg_2_normal (numpy.ndarray) – Outward unit normals of the two legs, shape (n, 3).

  • length_edge_m (float) – Length along the edge [m].

  • leg_dimension_m (float) – Leg height perpendicular to the edge [m].

  • n_tx2s (numpy.ndarray) – Tx-to-surface and surface-to-Rx unit directions, shape (n, 3).

  • n_s2rx (numpy.ndarray) – Tx-to-surface and surface-to-Rx unit directions, shape (n, 3).

  • wavelength_m (float) – Carrier wavelength [m].

Returns:

Per-sample dihedral RCS [m^2], shape (n,); 0 outside the wedge.

Return type:

numpy.ndarray

Summary¶

functions.functions is the project’s shared toolbox (imported as fn). It collects small geometry, propagation, and input/output helpers used across the simulator. The main groups:

These are utilities rather than physics, so they are summarised here rather than each given a full section; the docstrings in the source carry the per-function detail.

Module Assumptions and Limitations¶

  • VNC needs a valid state. build_vnc_frame returns None for a degenerate state (zero velocity or position, or position parallel to velocity); callers must handle that.

  • Nominal boresight is not exact nadir for eccentric motion. The VNC C axis is the component of position perpendicular to velocity. With the configured mounting, antenna \(+z\) points along \(-C\); this equals geocentric nadir for a circular orbit, but differs slightly when radial velocity is nonzero.

  • Ship shapes are idealised. ship_physics uses perfect conducting plates and a scalar dihedral peak with simple visibility. It omits full polarimetric angular response, component interference and rough-sea coupling; see Targets: base class and ship.

  • Local ellipsoid approximation. delta_lon/lat_from_distance use WGS-84 local radii of curvature. They convert a local east/north displacement, not an arbitrary long geodesic.

Validation and Tests¶

Test module

What it pins

tests/test_rotations.py

Quaternion-to-matrix, the VNC frame (orthonormal, degenerate cases), and the composed ECI-to-antenna rotation.

tests/test_functions.py

The geometry / time / distance helpers.

tests/test_ship_physics.py

Plate peak and sinc nulls, back-face culling, dihedral retroreflection peak, edge nulls, and wedge visibility. These are formula checks, not measured-ship validation.

ship_physics is also exercised end-to-end through tests/test_ship_target.py.

References¶

  • Vallado, D. A., Fundamentals of Astrodynamics and Applications, 4th ed., 2013 (orbit frames).

  • Knott, E., Schaeffer, J. & Tulley, M., Radar Cross Section, 2nd ed., SciTech, 2004 (plate / dihedral RCS).
